problem: The C-style header is cut off mid-expression: "for ((i=0; i. In the C-style header...". The condition and update parts of the header are missing, so the code is not valid and the sentence cannot be read.
fix: The C-style form uses arithmetic: for ((i=0; i<3; i++)); do echo $i; done. In the C-style header, i=0 runs once, i<3 is tested before each pass, and i++ runs after each pass.

where: Section 3, reading a file line by line
problem: The input redirection is missing, so the text reads "done . -r stops backslash processing, and  sends the file to standard input." The command has a stray period and the sentence has a blank where the redirection should be. A student cannot see how the file reaches read.
fix: To read a file line by line, use while IFS= read -r line; do ...; done < file. -r stops backslash processing, and < file sends the file to standard input.

problem: The text is truncated: "for ((i=1; i does arithmetic." The comparison and increment are missing, so the trap about the difference between the word-list for and the C-style for is unreadable.
fix: A for over words is not a C-style counter. for i in 1 2 3 assigns each word; for ((i=1; i<=3; i++)) does arithmetic.

problem: "1 is failure" suggests 1 is the only failure value. Failure is any non-zero status, for example 1, 2 or 127 (command not found).
fix: 0 is true and means success; any non-zero status (1, 2, 127, and so on) is false and means failure.
